## pluggable_component

```yaml
name: forecast
return_type: ForecastResult
signature_template: forecast(model, history, static_features, time_varying_features,
  graph, entity_ids, target_scaling_state, seed, *paradigm_extras_by_name) -> ForecastResult
contract:
  fixed_positional_args:
  - model
  - history
  - static_features
  - time_varying_features
  - graph
  - entity_ids
  - target_scaling_state
  seed_param: seed
  paradigm_extras_forwarding: by_name_from_config
  forbidden_param_names:
  - config
return_type_definition: 'ForecastResult is a dataclass defined in method/method.py
  with fields:

  - mean: torch.Tensor  # (N, K) expected value in original target units for N series
  over K future steps

  - variance: torch.Tensor  # (N, K) uncertainty in squared original target units
  (document the exact semantics: scale**2 vs true variance)

  - samples: torch.Tensor  # (num_samples, N, K) Monte Carlo draws in original target
  units

  - distribution_params: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]  # parameters with target-valued
  location/scale restored to original units; dimensionless params (e.g. Student-t
  df) stay unchanged

  '
rationale: "The pluggable takes a trained model, historical values, static\nper-series\
  \ features, known time-varying covariates, the inter-series\nstructure (graph adjacency\
  \ / edge index; None for methods without\none), the exact typed stable entity ids\
  \ for the series axis, and the\ntraining-only target-scaling state keyed by those\
  \ ids. It joins\nscales by typed identity rather than row position and uses the\
  \ fixed\nmethod.target_scaling.inverse_forecast_output helper to return every\n\
  target-valued field in the original target units: mean/location and\nsamples multiply\
  \ by scale, distribution scale multiplies by the\nabsolute scale, and variance multiplies\
  \ by squared scale. It must\nreturn distribution parameters or samples \u2014 not\
  \ just a point\nestimate \u2014 because the family's value is\ndecision-making under\
  \ uncertainty. samples must be genuine draws\n(measurable spread consistent with\
  \ the scale parameter), never\naliased conditional means. The seed parameter makes\
  \ sampling\nreproducible; num_samples is forwarded by name, never hardcoded.\n"
```

## notebook_layout

```yaml
description: 'Section structure for time-series forecasting notebooks. The protocol
  sections are load-bearing: chronology-preserving aggregation with an explicit missing-value
  policy, a held-out evaluation window that carries signal, visible training evidence,
  naive baselines, one machine-readable executed-evaluation record, and a deterministic
  presentation verdict derived from that record.

  '
sections:
- id: title
  title: Paper title (from spec.paper.title)
  kind: agnostic
- id: install
  title: '## 0. Install dependencies (first run only)'
  kind: agnostic
- id: setup
  title: '## 1. Setup'
  kind: agnostic
- id: parameters
  title: '## 2. Parameters'
  kind: agnostic
- id: setup_pieces
  title: '## 3. The setup pieces'
  kind: paradigm
  subsections:
  - id: data
    title: '### 3.1 Data'
    content: 'Load via the package''s load_data(). Print the realized shapes (N series,
      T steps, feature counts). Aggregation to the protocol''s time unit must key
      by year AND period (e.g. isocalendar year*100+week) so chronology survives,
      must state and apply an explicit missing-value policy (blank cells arrive as
      NaN from the loader), and must print where the target''s usable data ends when
      the tail is missing (public competition datasets withhold the target over their
      final period).

      '
  - id: structure
    title: '### 3.2 Inter-series structure'
    content: 'Build the inter-series structure the method uses (e.g. a similarity
      graph). Print its statistics (nodes, edges, average degree, isolated count).
      Omit this subsection for methods without relational structure.

      '
  - id: model
    title: '### 3.3 Model'
    content: 'Build the model. Print an architecture summary naming the encoder layers,
      decoder layers, and the output distribution head.

      '
  - id: training_protocol
    title: '### 3.4 Training protocol'
    content: "Explain optimizer, loss (distribution NLL), batching strategy, context\
      \ length, horizon, and the temporal split: training and the forecast's conditioning\
      \ context both end before the evaluation window. No code cell \u2014 training\
      \ runs in section 5.\n"
- id: method
  title: '## 4. The {method_name} method'
  kind: method_specific
- id: running
  title: '## 5. Training and forecasting end-to-end'
  kind: paradigm
  subsections:
  - id: train_loop
    title: '### 5.1 Training loop'
    content: 'Run training through the declared train_model entry and retain the fixed
      method.training_history record returned under the exact training_history key.
      A bare "Training complete." line or prose-parsed loss series is not training
      evidence. The time-window stride is its own quantity, never the series batch
      size. Emit exactly one compact, sorted-key, allow_nan=False JSON line prefixed
      `R2C_TARGET_SCALING_STATE_JSON: ` from the state returned by the declared fitting
      call, and exactly one line prefixed `R2C_TRAINING_HISTORY_JSON: ` from the returned
      history. Generated code writes neither pipeline-owned artifact.

      '
  - id: forecast
    title: '### 5.2 Forecasting'
    content: 'Call the pluggable forecast function conditioned on history that ends
      where training ended. Plot mean forecast with an uncertainty band from the samples
      against actual values for a few representative series; draw the actuals line
      only where actuals are finite, and say so when they are not.

      '
  - id: evaluation
    title: '### 5.3 Evaluation'
    content: 'Compute the paper''s metrics (e.g. RMSE, MAE, WMAPE) on the held-out
      window with explicit NaN discipline (assert finiteness; never let NaN propagate
      silently). From the executed actuals, model predictions, and pre-window history,
      emit exactly one JSON line prefixed `R2C_DEMO_EVALUATION_JSON: `. Its object
      carries literal schema_version `2.0.0` and one exact evaluation_protocol_role
      copied from comparison.evaluation_protocol.quantities, plus target_root, model_id,
      checkpoint_id, config_id, metric_id, units, aggregation, row_ids, evaluation_positions,
      actuals, finite_mask, model_predictions, model_metric, actual_values_id, finite_mask_id,
      and a comparators mapping keyed by predict_zero and repeat_last. It also carries
      a target_scaling_proof mapping with literal schema_version `1.0.0`, typed entity_ids
      and their exact entity_id_root, scaled_actuals and original_actuals with an
      explicit actual_output_role and actual_entity_axis, plus scaled_predictions
      and original_predictions with an explicit prediction_output_role and prediction_entity_axis.
      Preserve the executed array shape and identity order; never flatten, reshape,
      or infer an entity axis for this proof. Use `test_span` only when the executed
      evaluation is the typed protocol''s test-span role. Otherwise carry the exact
      role the typed protocol declares for that evaluation; do not infer a role from
      the window length, row count, a nearby numeric value, or prose. finite_mask
      is exactly the per-row finiteness mask of actuals: every finite actual is true
      and every JSON-null missing actual is false; it cannot select rows by model
      or comparator performance. Each comparator carries implementation, predictions,
      metric, row_ids, evaluation_positions, units, actual_values_id, and finite_mask_id.
      repeat_last also carries one value in input_values and one input position in
      input_positions per row, with every input position equal to the final position
      immediately before the complete evaluation window; a later horizon cannot reuse
      an earlier held-out actual and the producer cannot select an arbitrarily older
      weak persistence value. predict_zero may carry empty input_positions. Identity
      fields use the shared canonical recipe: prefix `sha256:` to SHA-256 over UTF-8
      compact JSON with sorted keys (`separators=(",", ":")`, `ensure_ascii=False`,
      `allow_nan=False`). actual_values_id hashes `{actuals, row_ids, units}`; finite_mask_id
      hashes `{finite_mask, row_ids}`. Represent masked missing values as JSON null.
      They are never prose labels. The pipeline recomputes model_metric and every
      comparator metric and requires numerical agreement within the shared deterministic
      floating-point tolerance. Print model, predict-zero, and repeat-last metrics
      beside one another. Then print one `Demo verdict:` presentation line derived
      from those executed objects: PASS only when the eligible model beats both required
      comparators under demo_skill; otherwise FAIL with the comparison reason. The
      notebook never declares evaluation validity: the pipeline joins the trusted
      split receipt, and printed PASS/FAIL is not evidence authority.

      '
- id: own_data
  title: '## 6. Use your own data'
  kind: agnostic
```

## demo_skill

```yaml
schema_version: 1.0.0
primary_metric:
  id: rmse
  direction: lower_is_better
  aggregation: root_mean_squared_error
  units: target_units
eligibility:
  minimum_finite_rows: 1
  require_nonzero_actuals: true
decision_policy: all_required
comparators:
- id: predict_zero
  role: degeneracy_floor
  implementation: predict_zero
  required: true
  absolute_margin: 0.0
  tolerance: 1.0e-12
- id: repeat_last
  role: minimum_competence
  implementation: repeat_last_pre_window
  required: true
  absolute_margin: 0.0
  tolerance: 1.0e-12
```

## smoke_bugs

```yaml
- id: tsf_nan_from_missing_values
  symptom: NaN loss or metrics, or a distribution-constraint error (Chi2/StudentT
    df constraint) mid-training or at evaluation.
  likely_cause: 'Blank cells in real tables become NaN at the loader (documented behavior),
    the notebook aggregates with += and no missing-value policy, and NaN flows into
    training targets or ground truth. Fix at the aggregation seam. Sanitizing the
    model''s inputs (np.nan_to_num inside forecast) is the band-aid shape: it turns
    a loud crash into a silent NaN metric.

    '
  fix: r2c-notebook-generator
  status: seed
- id: tsf_withheld_target_tail
  symptom: Metrics are NaN or identically zero on the last-K evaluation window while
    the model and weights are entirely finite.
  likely_cause: 'The public source withholds the target over its final period (competition
    layout), so the nominal axis outlives the usable extent and the held-out tail
    carries no ground truth. Evaluate on the last window that has data; state where
    usable data ends.

    '
  fix: r2c-notebook-generator
  status: seed
- id: tsf_declared_vs_realized_dims
  symptom: RuntimeError 'expected N, got M' at the decoder or LSTM input, typically
    two layers away from the cause.
  likely_cause: "Declared context/feature dimensions disagree with the bundle's realized\
    \ axis (e.g. 10 declared lags over a 4-step axis, silently clamped into a width-4\
    \ slice). The root is bundle axis coverage or a silent clamp \u2014 validate declared\
    \ dimensions against realized data and raise with the arithmetic in the message.\n"
  fix: r2c-architecture-coder
  status: seed
- id: tsf_unconstrained_distribution_params
  symptom: 'NaN loss or sampling errors: scale is non-positive or degrees-of-freedom
    drifts below its support.'
  likely_cause: The output head emits raw logits for scale/df without softplus plus
    a floor, or the loss does not constrain them.
  fix: r2c-architecture-coder
  status: seed
- id: tsf_graph_no_edges
  symptom: Relational encoder produces constant or zero embeddings; all nodes isolated
    (graph-based methods only).
  likely_cause: Similarity threshold too high for the demo's sparse features yields
    a graph with no edges; aggregation over empty neighborhoods returns zeros.
  fix: r2c-method-coder
  status: seed
- id: tsf_string_cast_real_columns
  symptom: 'ValueError: could not convert string to float during data preparation.'
  likely_cause: Real tables carry string ids, dates, and categorical columns; a blanket
    float cast dies on them. Use the loader's typed columns and parse dates explicitly.
  fix: r2c-notebook-generator
  status: seed
```
